analysis.title: Tech Stress Persists As Small Caps Come Roaring Back
key_insights: NDX remains in the same trading range it has held since May. Support is at the lower end of the range, around 29k in futures, with the 200-day moving average about 500 points below that. The note sees little reason to get excited until the range breaks in either direction.
Tech volatility remains elevated relative to the broad market. VXN carries a persistent premium over both VIX and RVX.
CDS stress continues to weigh on tech. The note says a sustainable bull move looks difficult until credit stress eases, and recommends watching CDS spreads closely.
The Russell fell below its 200-day moving average earlier this month and has since reclaimed it. Small caps have been the big outperformers over the past few weeks.

The Market Ear's early October note cited GS data on extreme Russell positioning: systematic exposure at the 7th percentile and record leveraged-fund shorts in Russell 2000 futures. GS flagged the potential for a powerful squeeze if yields reversed lower, and the note says the call looks well timed.
GS flagged aggressive hedge fund shorts near the recent Russell lows, particularly among momentum-driven strategies. The open question is how much of that short exposure has already been covered.

The note's conclusion is that the more interesting trade may be about who leads from here rather than overall market direction. As long as tech struggles to regain momentum, small-cap relative outperformance deserves attention.
